short: Chile's AI bill (Boletín 16821-19, merged with 15869-19) passed the Chamber of Deputies on 13 October 2025 and was approved in general by the Senate's Future Challenges committee on 26 October 2026, with indications due 4 December 2026. It copies the EU four-tier model with fines up to 20,000 UTM. Law No. 21.719 rewrites data protection.
title: Chile AI Laws
subtitle: An AI bill in the Senate, and a new data protection law
body_html:
Status at a glance

AI bill pending. Chile's bill to regulate artificial intelligence systems (Regula los sistemas de inteligencia artificial, Boletín 16821-19, merged with Boletín 15869-19) was approved in detail by the Chamber of Deputies on 13 October 2025 and moved to the Senate on 14 October 2025, where the committee on Future Challenges, Science, Technology and Innovation approved it in general on 26 October 2026, with indications proposed for 4 December 2026. The government has kept a simple urgency on it, renewed monthly, most recently on 1 September 2026. Chile's data protection law was rewritten by Law No. 21.719, which creates a Personal Data Protection Agency. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Senate's legislative record service and the Library of Congress (BCN).

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberStageIn force
Bill regulating AI systemsBoletín 16821-19, merged with 15869-19Chamber approval 13 October 2025; Senate committee stage from 14 October 2025No
Law regulating the protection and processing of personal data and creating the Personal Data Protection AgencyLey No. 21.719Promulgated 25 November 2024; Diario Oficial 13 December 2024Its amendments apply from the first day of the twenty-fourth month after publication (first transitional provision)

Who regulates and enforces

  • Personal Data Protection Agency, created by Law No. 21.719: the future data protection authority.
  • The AI bill's enforcer could not be read on an official source.

Scope and reach

No AI statute is in force. The bill's text could not be opened: the Chamber's and the Senate's document pages answered this crawler 403, so its scope is not stated here.

Core obligations

  • None under an AI law yet. Law No. 21.719 governs AI that processes personal data once its amendments apply.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Under the AI bill, if enactedNot stated: the bill text could not be read on an official sourceBoletín 16821-19
Under Law No. 21.719Not stated: the official text's sanctions title did not renderLey No. 21.719Personal Data Protection Agency

What is coming next

  • The Senate committee's first report on the AI bill.
  • The application of Law No. 21.719's amendments, on the first day of the twenty-fourth month after its publication on 13 December 2024, which this site reads as 1 December 2026.

What the bill says, and where it stands in the Senate

On 26 October 2026 the Senate committee on Future Challenges, Science, Technology and Innovation approved the merged bill in general, unanimously as CNN Chile reported, which means it endorsed the idea of legislating but left every article open. The committee proposed 4 December 2026 as the deadline for indications, the date by which the Ministry of Science is also expected to table the government's own amendments, and that deadline awaits ratification by the Senate floor. The committee had earlier heard the Ministry of Science and civil society witnesses through the first half of 2026, and the government withdrew and re-entered its urgency on 20 January 2026 before the monthly renewals noted above. These facts are from the Chilean press and the Senate's own news service, not from the committee's minutes.

The text that left the Chamber of Deputies on 13 October 2025 copies the EU AI Act's architecture. It sorts AI systems into four tiers: unacceptable risk, which is prohibited; high risk, with mandatory standards on data governance, documentation, human oversight and incident reporting; limited risk, with transparency duties; and the rest, unregulated. It creates a mandatory protocol for reporting failures or harm caused by an AI system, gives the Consejo para la Transparencia a widened role, and leaves the Secretaría de Gobierno Digital in the Ministry of Finance to issue guidance for the public sector. A technical council would propose the lists of high-risk and limited-risk systems and the law would be evaluated every three years. Sanctions run on three levels: up to 5,000 UTM for minor infringements such as transparency failures, up to 10,000 UTM for serious ones such as breaking the high-risk rules, and up to 20,000 UTM for the most serious, including using a prohibited system. At the November 2026 UTM value that top band is roughly CLP 1.4 billion. Regulatory sandboxes are offered as the counterweight.

Chilean commentators, including columns in El Mostrador and El Dínamo in 2026, argue the bill's sanctions outrun its institutions, since no dedicated AI regulator is funded and the new Personal Data Protection Agency under Law No. 21.719 is itself still being set up. Whatever the Senate does with the articles, the earliest realistic date for a law is 2027, after a third reading in the Chamber if the Senate changes the text.

Last verified

4 November 2026, against the sources above. The committee's 26 October 2026 approval in general and the 4 December deadline are as CNN Chile and El Dínamo report them; the committee minutes were not read. The bill's tiers and UTM bands are as the Chamber's news service and law-firm summaries describe the text that left the Chamber, and may change in the Senate. The CLP equivalent is this site's arithmetic. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the government's 2026 indications and the fine amounts of Law No. 21.719.
